assessments.reasoning: I retrieved Oracle's governing Java SE 21 JLS from its edition-specific HTTPS locator and matched the frozen source SHA-256 before inspecting every listed paragraph. JLS §11.2 frames coverage as a throws entry for the checked class or a superclass. Section 11.2.3 imposes a compile-time error on the method or constructor body in the frozen uncovered case. The subject is the result of exception analysis on the body, including the effect of a handler or a finally block under §11.2.2. The targeted comparison found no applicable contradiction.

challenge.method: Compare an uncovered checked exception with the same class or superclass declared, an unrelated class declared, a matching catch, an unchecked exception, and an intervening finally block that cannot complete normally. Read the separate lambda and initializer rules in §11.2.3.
challenge.results: An unrelated declaration leaves the checked class uncovered. A matching catch or a finally that cannot complete normally can remove the original checked class from the static result for the inner try. An unchecked class is exempt from this rule. The clause-present comparisons use clauses naming classes, as the record specifies.

limitations: The verdict is confined to the stated class-only or absent throws clause and to method and constructor body analysis. Lambda and initializer rules are outside this claim.
